title: Delimiter resilience and graceful truncation semantics for streamed structured outputs
creator: Aisha Kline
description: Problem: Clients using streamed structured JSON responses (tool/function calls or ndjson-like chunks) see frequent failure modes when the stream is truncated mid-object or when model-inserted delimiters collide with content. This causes incorrect tool-call invocation, parse failures, or silent data loss. Goal: implement a compatibility-first, conservative server-side policy and a client guidance/spec so both old and new SDKs handle truncation, escaping and retries deterministically.
background: We already have several tickets addressing stream resume, escaping, and repair heuristics but they assume either full control of client or a newer framing format. Many SDK users are on older versions or use raw HTTP streaming. We need a server-side policy that degrades gracefully for those clients while enabling a new explicit handshake/framing mode for upgraded SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime inserts a single, stable 'chunk trailer' sentinel when it decides to end a chunk due to SSE/connection close or truncation; this trailer is backwards-compatible with existing streaming clients (treated as text) and detectable by new SDKs.
Tool-calling parser in SDKs can distinguish: complete JSON object, partial JSON (truncated), and escaped-delimiter occurrences with >95% detection in fuzz tests.
Server exposes a 'stream-semantics' header in streaming responses (values: legacy, safe-framing, handshake) and behavior matches spec in confluence doc.

End-to-end tests (runtime + js/python SDK) for truncation + retry scenarios pass in CI with deterministic outcomes: either successful resume, graceful fallback to NDJSON-per-line, or a clear error with diagnostics for retries.
No regression (measured by existing integration tests) in latency tail and token throughput (+/- 3%).
design_decisions: We selected a layered approach: 1) Default legacy mode (no client changes) but runtime will append a short printable trailer sequence — e.g. '<<END_CHUNK:HEXCRC>>' when closing a chunk. This is unlikely to collide with model output and acts as a weak checksum. 2) A 'safe-framing' mode for new SDKs where server and client use an explicit length-prefixed frame or multibyte sentinel and a 4-byte CRC32 for chunk integrity. 3) A 'handshake' mode where the client announces support for idempotent toolcall replays and semantic checkpoints, enabling server to emit checkpoint tokens that map to KV-cache boundaries for safe retry. Trade-offs: the trailer approach is weak but low-friction; length-prefixed frames are robust but add overhead and require SDK updates; handshake adds complexity to router/orchestration but yields best reliability for Dedicated/Private customers.
implementation_plan: Server: implement trailer generator in runtime (C++ layer in serving runtime) that appends trailer only when the model stream terminates or runtime triggers truncation. Expose new response header 'x-rw-stream-semantics'. Add config flag per-tenant to select safe-framing/handshake. SDKs: detect trailer patterns and treat trailing chunk as indicator; new SDK versions implement length-prefixed frames and handshake flows. Backwards compat: legacy clients ignore header and treat trailer as text. Steps: 1) RFC and confluence doc, 2) minimal runtime change to append trailer (feature flag off by default), 3) rollout enabling feature flag for internal test tenants, 4) SDK updates (js/python) to opt into safe-framing, 5) enable default safe-framing for new tenants after 2 weeks of internal testing.
testing: Unit tests for trailer generation and CRC calculation. Fuzz harness feeding randomized JSON + model-like continuations to verify detection rate. Integration tests in staging: simulate network truncation, connection resets, and intentional mid-object truncation; verify SDKs produce one of: resume-and-reload, do-retry-with-idempotency, or surface clear error. Add benchmarks to ensure append-only trailer adds <0.2% CPU overhead and <1% tail-latency change.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag implementation in runtime (internal only). Phase 1: enable trailer for a small % of hosted traffic (internal dev tenants). Phase 2: roll out safe-framing SDKs to customers via release notes and migration docs. Phase 3: turn on safe-framing by default for new tenants; existing tenants can opt-in or stay legacy for 6 months. Monitor errors for parsing failures, tool mis-invocations, and customer tickets.
risks: Trailer collision if models intentionally or accidentally emit the trailer sequence (mitigation: use hex CRC and rarely used delimiters and fall back to length-prefixed for handshake mode). Increased complexity in Dedicated/Private upgrades due to per-tenant flags. Potential client fragmentation if many customers don't upgrade SDKs; we mitigate with a long compatibility window and server-side conservative defaults.
open_questions: What exact sentinel pattern minimizes collision risk across languages/encodings?
Should the runtime compute CRC of the raw bytes or the UTF-8 codepoints?
How to coordinate retries for multi-request toolcall sequences that cross chunk boundaries?
Do we need a schema-level marker for tool-call boundaries in addition to chunk-level trailers?
notes: Ran a short experiment on staging with an ad-hoc trailer '<<END_CHUNK-A1B2>>'; observed 12% reduction in tooling-related parse errors for raw HTTP clients. Logged CPU delta ~0.15% for trailer append. See staging dashboard for details.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial RFC posted to Confluence. Feedback from Reviewers (SRE, SDK): favor length-prefixed for JS SDK but keep trailer for Python due to wide raw-HTTP usage.
2026-03-10: Fuzzing harness results: 96.3% detection of truncation when trailer present; false-positive rate 0.8% on corpora sampled from real outputs.
2026-03-12: Design review with SDK leads. Agreement: ship trailer as low-friction compatibility shim and separately release SDK safe-framing in next minor.
2026-03-13: Feature-flag merged behind admin toggle (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/409). Enabled for internal test tenants.
Pending: coordinate release notes and migration guide with Docs (owner: Naomi Park).
